fatal_errors: The proposed AlNbTiZr medium-entropy coating is materially different from the target AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy coating, omitting the Cr and Ta needed for the reported protective mixed Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 layer.

The cited evidence concerns corrosion of AlNbTiZr on N36 alloy in pressurized-water-reactor operating conditions, not 1000-1100 °C flowing-steam oxidation or neutron irradiation; it therefore does not support the stated LOCA and irradiation claims.
The predicted retention of neutron and mechanical properties is asserted without supporting evidence.
The proposed Nb2Zr6O17/ZrO2 mediator conflicts with the target mechanism and does not establish the high-temperature steam barrier invoked in the hypothesis.
explanation: The response addresses the general coating-design problem and correctly identifies an intermediate aluminum content near 10 at.% as potentially optimal. It also proposes measurable morphology, oxidation, adhesion, and mechanical endpoints with an explicit falsification threshold. However, it reconstructs a different literature system: RF-sputtered AlNbTiZr on N36 rather than approximately 4 μm DC-sputtered AlTiCrZrNbTa on polished Zircaloy-4. Consequently, it misses the target compositional controls, Al-free baseline, exact steam exposures, nonmonotonic failure at at least 17 at.% Al, mixed Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 barrier, and Cr/Ti enrichment and intermetallic-based mechanism. Most importantly, evidence obtained under PWR-water corrosion conditions is extrapolated to severe-accident steam and irradiation without validation. The experiment is only moderately discriminating because temperature, exposure time, steam flow, coating thickness, irradiation dose, and compositional comparison groups are unspecified, while oxidation and irradiation are bundled into one test.
